maps.credit: A new map of the Cherokee Nation, 1760, hmap1760k5, Hargrett Rare Book and Manuscript Library, University of Georgia Libraries; presented by the Digital Library of Georgia. Engraved by Thomas Kitchin.
maps.annotation: Kitchin’s 1760 engraving names Cherokee towns and rivers. Its margin credits an unidentified Indigenous draught, mediated through a London magazine publication. Compare this historical representation with Cherokee accounts; it does not establish present government boundaries.
maps.perspective: Colonial engraving / mediated Indigenous geographic knowledge

profileConnections.name: Cherokee
profileConnections.evidence: The actual title identifies the Cherokee Nation; the scan labels Cherokee towns and rivers. The archive independently indexes Cherokee Nation history/maps.
profileConnections.scope: Historical Cherokee-country representation; no exclusive assignment to one present Cherokee government.

inspection.scope: Read the complete actual archive record and manifest. Inspected the complete downloaded 3065x2372 scan at original resolution, including the cartouche, town/river labels and bottom engraver/source credit.
inspection.observedFeatures: Landscape sheet; named towns along rivers; mountain symbols; scale; decorated lower-left title; source/engraver credit below the map.
inspection.limits: No georeferencing, modern town equivalence, boundary inference or identification of the unnamed draught maker.

editorialNotes: Same historical work as an unpublished University of Alabama lead, but this is a newly inspected accessible primary copy with item-specific rights.
Avoid a London Magazine volume number: the DLG record's volume23 conflicts with the LOC record's volume29. Date1760 and title are secure; no volume asserted.
Do not describe the engraving as an unmediated Indigenous original.

maps.credit: Second Seminole War, Okefenokee region manuscript map, ms4209, Box1 Folder1, Hargrett Rare Book and Manuscript Library, University of Georgia Libraries; presented by the Digital Library of Georgia.
maps.annotation: Attributed to Greenleaf Dearborn, this 1837–1838 manuscript depicts military forts and routes around the Okefenokee during the Second Seminole War. It records an Army viewpoint, rather than Seminole territorial authority or present boundaries.

profileConnections.name: Seminole
profileConnections.evidence: The actual record identifies the Second Seminole War and indexes Seminole Indians/Florida and Seminole wars. The scan shows military routes and forts in the region.
profileConnections.scope: A military representation connected with Seminole history; not Seminole-authored, a homeland map, or evidence of current jurisdiction.

inspection.scope: Read the complete actual item record and rights. Downloaded the actual two-page PDF, rendered both pages at 2200px, and visually inspected both: map face and verso sketches.
inspection.observedFeatures: Handwritten map around the Okefenokee with wetlands, streams, fort symbols and dotted routes; verso bears a short map label and sketches.
inspection.limits: No full handwriting transcription, exact sensitive-place coordinates, present boundaries or certainty beyond the archive's author attribution.

editorialNotes: Display title is descriptive; preserve the archive's literal title Map in metadata.

exclusionsAndLimits: Compared against all12 existing catalogue items; neither addition duplicates an existing published item.
